articles.title: Low-field proton relaxation and rapid resonant thermalization in hyperpolarized glasses
articles.description: Spin hyperpolarization enables new applications in areas spanning from nuclear magnetic resonance to quantum sensing. These applications often require a sample transfer from the point of hyperpolarization to the point of use. During this transfer, the sample is typically exposed to fields below 0.1 T. Here, we investigate low-field proton relaxation in nitroxide-doped frozen glasses. These glasses are widely used in dynamic nuclear polarization (DNP), where polarization is transferred from free electron spins to nuclear spins. Using fast-field-cycling (FFC) experiments, we identify two relaxation pathways. Above ~0.25 T, we establish a heuristic description of radical-induced relaxation, which is modeled using a radical-mediated triple-spin-flip mechanism. Below ~0.25 T we report an unexpected process that we call rapid resonant thermalization (RRT). RRT occurs on a millisecond timescale and is observed when radicals are present, but importantly also in the absence of radicals when deuterium is present. Our findings will guide the development of improved transfer protocols and sample formulations for preserving hyperpolarization.
